newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks recover but sentiment remains grim.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks recover but sentiment remains grim.

text.p: Thailand's key index finished in positive territory on Tuesday after a week of downward spirals and new lows, but analysts said the rebound was technical and not a sign of improved sentiment.
The Stock Exchange of Thailand index ended six straight days of falls and edged slightly above the psychological 600-point level to end up 8.06 points, or 1.36 percent, at 600.24.
About 4.2 billion baht ($161.5 million) worth of shares changed hands -- the busiest day in about three weeks.
"I was expecting it to go up today," said one analyst. "I believe this is a technical rebound of a severely oversold market."
Brokers said bargain hunters were picking up blue chip stocks following a plunge in their prices.
"We all know the shares are very low already. So investors may think today is a good time to buy," said one broker at Wall Street Finance.
Analysts say there may be more upside to come in the next day or two.
"It's a good feeling to see the index ending above 600 points. But market sentiment remains cautious on economic worries," said another broker at local investment house.

Concerns over a slowing economy, poor first quarter results, beleaguered property and finance sectors, and uncertainty over the scope of the government's efforts to improve the situation have all been blamed for the market's recent falls to the lowest levels in more than six years.
Continued speculation over the possible resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan added to the uncertainty in the market.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Tuesday said Amnuay was staying in his position, and reaffirmed his six-month old government was doing all it could to help the economy.
"We have had high economic growth for the past 10 years so there must be some overheating and adjustment," Chavalit said after the weekly cabinet meeting.
Private economists predict the Thai economy will grow about five percent this year -- a sharp difference from the average nine percent growth the country enjoyed over the past decade.

Analysts said the bourse shrugged off news that Thailand's biggest merger of financial institutions between Thai Danu Bank and Finance One Plc had been turned into a takeover with the bank now acquiring cash-strapped Finance One.
"It was not a big surprise...," said one analyst. "But there are concerns about what this holds for other blue-chip finance stocks."
The Thai government has urged finance companies to merge to become stronger and overcome a current crisis of confidence in the sector.

A four-year property slump has threatened the stability of Thailand's banking and finance sector, which has extended about 800 billion baht of loans to property developers. At least 20 percent of those loans are thought to be non-performing.
